The docs did the heavy lifting here, and the failure-prevention is attributable to specific passages. doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Tag_Processor — 'Building markup from a template' section (lines 158-182)
doc_gaps.problem: The template example walks next_token() from the matched tag onward and grabs the FIRST #text node, but never states that this assumes the desired text node is the first one reached. In templates with multiple text-bearing elements or whitespace/text between elements, the first #text may not be the intended target. Two of three subjects copied the unguarded loop without realizing it depends on template layout.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a sentence noting that the next_token() loop stops at the first #text node, so when a template has more than one text location, either order the template so the target text comes first, or narrow the walk first with next_tag() to position the cursor on the intended element before scanning for its #text child.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain that an empty element has no text node to replace, but do not state the corollary failure mode: calling set_modifiable_text when the cursor is NOT on a #text-bearing token (or when no placeholder exists) silently returns false / does nothing rather than erroring. A subject who forgot the placeholder would get a silent no-op with no diagnostic.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Document set_modifiable_text's return value and the no-op behavior explicitly: it returns false when there is no matched modifiable-text token, and makes no change. Pair this with the existing placeholder rule so readers connect 'no placeholder' to 'silent no-op'.

doc_gaps.problem: The critical rule that NEWLY added attributes are emitted sorted by name (not call order), while attributes already present in the source preserve their position, is only mentioned in passing in the template section (line 162) and not stated at the set_attribute method itself where readers look first. Tasks with a required attribute order depend entirely on this fact.
doc_gaps.suggestion: State the ordering behavior directly in the set_attribute docblock: updating an existing attribute preserves its position; adding a new attribute places it after existing attributes sorted by name. Cross-reference the template technique (seed empty attributes in source) as the way to control output order.
